findings.reason: the node must know which mesh it is sizing, and if production rebuilds the mesh then G must be rebuilt and its measured compile and memory cost re-taken, which changes what §3 and §4 each own.
findings.text: §3's done-when builds and sizes G over "the 1696-cell WEST mesh", but the plan never names where that mesh comes from: the production mesh is §4's (`nova/biot/magnetisation.py`, "Mesh it without slivers … quality triangles or merged quads") and §4 declares depends-on s3, so the only mesh available to §3 is the §1 prototype's `mesh(region, size)` in scripts/prototypes/iron_magnetisation/magnetisation.py:48, which §3 does not cite; and because §4 may change the cell shape and §5 adds graded refinement, the 1696-cell count and the 3392-square shape whose compile and warm times §3 records do not describe the production matrix

findings.reason: an implementer must either drop ψ from G (and §6/§7 then needs it from somewhere else) or build a non-square matrix, so the wrong reading lands a differently shaped object than the plan specifies and the compile and memory gate measures it.
findings.text: §3 defines G as "B_R, B_Z and ψ at targets per unit M_R and M_Z" but its done-when (2) at line 243 requires "that 3392-square Gram", and 2N×2N = 3392 holds only for B_R and B_Z on 1696 cells (the prototype's `interaction` returns exactly that, scripts/prototypes/iron_magnetisation/magnetisation.py:133), so carrying ψ at the same targets gives 5088×3392 and the node cannot satisfy both statements

findings.reason: without a stated rule §3 can pick a width that silently fails the 1e-10 target §2 established, and the reciprocal-ε tolerance means the gate would still be self-consistent while measuring the wrong accuracy.
findings.text: §2 records "the best attainable error and the ε that gives it recorded per slope", but neither §2 nor §3 states how the production G chooses the strip width ε: a 1696-cell mesh carries edges at several slopes, one global ε cannot be the per-slope optimum, and §3's agreement tolerance is defined as the host's reversed-order spread which "amplifies any change in summation order by about 1/ε" (line 240–241), so an arbitrary ε moves both the matrix's accuracy and the gate's tolerance
